scope: Product Admin category-bound GraphQL fallback read public error boundary

findings.finding: Five category-bound Product Admin reads preserve native server functions as the first path but returned the final GraphqlHttpError from their GraphQL fallback without a Product-owned public mapper. Http and Graphql variants could therefore carry status text or server messages into UI resources.

The smallest compatible fix adds explicit final wrappers in catalog_transport. Each wrapper creates one correlation context before invoking the unchanged native-first compatibility executor and maps only a final returned error.

The compatibility executor still calls native_server_adapter first and calls graphql_adapter only after native failure. The new wrapper adds no retry, second fallback, duplicate owner call, or transport-selection change.

Private diagnostics retain the typed GraphqlHttpError and record only token presence plus tenant, product, category, and locale character lengths. Effective-form product and category identifiers remain separate shape fields; raw values are not structured fields.

The existing primary-read guard counts its original five primary mappers plus the catalog-options mapper. New category wrappers intentionally use a distinct source marker so the prior source contract remains valid while the focused category guard locks the five new mappings.

preserved: absence of new retry or fallback paths
